subject: Hosting scope and pen-test evidence for Acme Analytics — mapping, roles, remediation ETA
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <s.lim@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Team <sec-team@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test deliverables + scope mapping request

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the quick onboarding this week. As part of Acme Analytics' procurement and security review we need three things to close our internal checklist: a) a clear articulation of which Redwood components will be in-scope for an external penetration test depending on hosting mode (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC, On‑prem); b) redacted or full pen-test reports (we can accept redacted if there are NDAs to sign); and c) current remediation status for any medium/high findings from your most recent assessment.

Specific asks from our side:
- Mapping table: for each deployment type, list components you consider in-scope (runtime, control plane, CI/CD, customer data storage, KV cache persistence, logging/telemetry).
- Confirmation whether customer-supplied models and embeddings are included in the scope for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Evidence: summary report (redacted), timeline for when full report can be shared under NDA, and any compensating controls for outstanding findings.

I've attached our questionnaire to help guide the mapping. Can you confirm an owner and an expected timeline? We're targeting a vendor review decision by Sept 24.

Best,
Sarah Lim
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme-PT-Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lim <s.lim@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test deliverables + scope mapping request

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear checklist. I'm taking lead on coordinating the artifacts with our security and product teams. High-level answers up front, details below and in the attached redacted summary.

Summary (short):
- Hosted API: In-scope for Redwood-managed runtime, API gateway, authentication/authorization services, and multi-tenant isolation layers. Customer data flows through shared runtime; customer models hosted via the Hosted API (bringing your own model) are considered data assets and are not subject to Redwood-managed runtime tests unless specifically requested.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): In-scope includes the dedicated GPU pool, our serving runtime on that pool, and associated storage endpoints we provide. Customer-managed VM host-level components (hypervisor/host OS) are out-of-scope — those are managed by our cloud provider.
- Private/VPC: In-scope is our runtime image and control plane connectors running inside the customer's VPC, plus any Redwood-managed connectors (e.g., private endpoints). The customer controls network egress rules; components running in the customer's network that Redwood does not manage are excluded.
- On-premise: Redwood only provides a packaging artifact; on-prem deployments are primarily customer-managed. Redwood can support a joint test but the onus and scheduling is with the customer and their local ops. Redwood-managed components that we shipped as part of the on-prem bundle (update service, agent) would be in-scope if the customer requests a joint assessment.

I've attached a redacted summary report to this message (see below). For the full report we require an executed NDA; once signed we can share the non-public findings and the full technical appendix.

Owner & next steps:
- Owner: KarThik Iyer (Security) — will produce a per-mode scope matrix and remediation table by Sept 14.
- Provide NDA: We will email an NDA template for your legal team (expect within 24 business hours).

ETA: KarThik's scope matrix and the redacted summary (attached) — Sept 14. Full report under NDA — typically 3 business days after NDA is signed.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-PT-Summary-redacted.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

2) KV cache: does Redwood persist per-tenant KV caches to durable storage across restarts in any hosting mode? If so, where are those encrypted and who holds the keys?

A short tech note answers both items will speed our review.

From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lim <s.lim@acme-analytics.com>, Oliver Cho <oliver@thirdpartysec.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: model artifacts and KV cache persistence (scope details)

Hi Sarah/Oliver —

Technical clarifications and explicit scope apportionment per hosting mode: see bullets below. I've also included remediation status for outstanding items from our last internal assessment.

Hosted API (shared runtime):
- Persistent storage: BYO-model weights are NOT persisted to shared disk in the multi-tenant Hosted runtime. Models are streamed into RAM and served from memory; ephemeral cached artifacts are removed on session termination. We do have a short-lived in-memory KV cache with optional TTL; no durable persistence to block/object storage for tenant KV in Hosted mode.
- Keys: control plane keys and secrets for Hosted are stored in our KMS (Redwood-managed). Customers can enable customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private via KMS integration (listed in the matrix).

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Persistent storage: Workspace-level artifacts (model uploads for a given customer) are stored on encrypted block volumes attached to the dedicated pool. These volumes are encrypted at rest with keys managed per-customer if customer requests CMK. Redwood manages the runtime software; the cloud hypervisor and host OS are managed by the cloud provider (excluded from Redwood pen-test scope).
- KV cache: Dedicated can be configured to persist caches to encrypted block storage; persistence is opt-in and must be requested during provisioning.

Private / VPC-hosted:
- Everything running inside the customer VPC that the customer manages is considered out-of-scope for Redwood's standalone pen-test. Redwood-managed connectors, images, and the control-plane connectors are in-scope if they run Redwood binaries. For private deployments we will provide the bundle-level CVE and hardening checklist; joint testing is recommended.

On-prem:
- On-prem deployments are customer-managed. Redwood can support a joint test engagement and provide instrumentation and guidance; test scheduling and host-level remediation are handled by the customer's infra team.

Remediation status (summary):
- HIGH (1): No open HIGH findings from the last 3rd-party test.
- MEDIUM (3): Two have mitigation in place; one (SDK deserialization hardening) is scheduled for fix and deployment by Sept 22 (release pipeline in PR stage).
- LOW/INFO: Items tracked in our backlog and will be closed in the next two sprints.

Deliverables we will provide by Sept 14:
- Per-mode scope matrix (CSV)
- Redacted summary report (PDF) — already attached in Jonas' message
- List of control mappings (SOC 2 / SIG references) — link to Drive below after NDA.

If Acme wants the full technical appendix with proof-of-exploit detail we'll need the NDA executed; we will also coordinate a short call between your assessor and our runtime engineers (30–45 minutes).

Regards,
KarThik Iyer
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
